about: AI lending marketplace that uses machine learning to assess credit risk, connecting consumers who want personal, auto and home equity loans with partner banks and credit unions. Earns referral and platform fees from lenders, and has originated tens of billions of dollars in loans. Headquartered in San Mateo, California, with an operations hub in Columbus, Ohio; founded 2012. Listed on Nasdaq (UPST). Shares volatile with interest rate cycles. B2B2C model: banks are customers, with modest consumer brand awareness in the United States.

wiki.title: Upstart Holdings
wiki.text: Upstart is a lending platform based in San Mateo, California. It was first launched in April 2012 with an Income Share Agreement (ISA) product, which enabled individuals to raise money by contracting to share a percent of their future income. In May 2014, Upstart pivoted away from this product and toward the personal loan marketplace. With this pivot, Upstart began offering a traditional 3-year loan, and has since expanded to offer a 5-year loan product as well.

about: Software company providing IT asset management, software license optimisation, cloud cost management (FinOps) and software vulnerability tools, used by enterprises to control technology spend. Customers are large enterprises and managed service providers worldwide. Headquartered in Itasca, Illinois; founded 1987. Private equity owned, with Thoma Bravo having bought it in 2020 and Vista Equity Partners among earlier backers. B2B brand known to IT leaders, with little consumer awareness, though it sponsors some events and sporting links.

wiki.title: Flexera
wiki.text: Flexera is a global enterprise software company based in Itasca, Illinois. It provides technology spend and risk intelligence solutions. Its core offerings are built around its Flexera One platform and a specialized division for software producers called Revenera.

about: Operator of Upbit, South Korea's largest cryptocurrency exchange, plus the Lounge blockchain platform and related digital asset services. Customers are retail crypto traders in Korea and Southeast Asia, with revenue from trading fees. Headquartered in Seoul; founded 2012. Unlisted, with a planned merger into Naver Financial announced in late 2025 through a share swap valued around 10 trillion won. Strong consumer brand in Korean crypto and a sponsor in esports and entertainment.

wiki.title: Upbit
wiki.text: Upbit is a South Korean cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2017. It is operated by Dunamu, which is one of the highest-valued startups in South Korea.

about: Chinese artificial intelligence lab founded in 2023 and funded by the hedge fund High-Flyer, which released the DeepSeek-V3 and R1 open-weight language models in late 2024 and early 2025, achieving high performance at low cost and drawing global attention. Offers a chatbot app, an API and open models. Headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. Privately held, with founder Liang Wenfeng. Very strong awareness among consumers and developers, but sensitive political and data-privacy context.

wiki.title: DeepSeek
wiki.text: Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd., doing business as DeepSeek, is a Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) company that develops open weights large language models (LLMs). Based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, DeepSeek is owned and funded by High-Flyer, a Chinese hedge fund.

wiki.text: In Greek mythology, Prometheus is a Titan who is responsible for creating and aiding humanity in its earliest days. He defied the Olympian gods by stealing fire from them and giving it to humanity.

wiki.title: Atom
wiki.what: Smallest unit of a chemical element
wiki.text: Atoms are the basic particles of the chemical elements and the fundamental building blocks of matter. An atom consists of a nucleus of protons and generally neutrons, surrounded by an electromagnetically bound swarm of electrons. The chemical elements are distinguished from each other by the number of protons that are in their atoms. For example, any atom that contains 11 protons is sodium, and any atom that contains 29 protons is copper. Atoms with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons are called isotopes of the same element.

about: Digital Edge is an Asia-focused data center platform that builds and operates carrier-neutral data centers in Indonesia, India, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam and elsewhere, backed by Stonepeak. Customers are cloud, internet and enterprise companies. Headquartered in Singapore; formed 2020. Funding is about 3.8 billion dollars including debt. Privately held. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer visibility.

about: DigitalOcean is a US cloud platform offering simple virtual servers called Droplets, managed databases, Kubernetes and GPU compute to developers, startups and small businesses. Revenue near 800 million dollars from about 600,000 customers. Headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, previously New York; founded 2011. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (DOCN). Developer-focused B2B brand, known in tech circles, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: DigitalOcean
wiki.text: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc. is an American multinational technology company and cloud service provider. The company is headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, US, with 15 globally distributed data centers. DigitalOcean provides developers, startups, and SMBs with cloud infrastructure-as-a-service platforms.

about: Lenskart is an Indian eyewear company selling prescription glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses through an online platform and a chain of over 2,000 owned and franchised stores in India and overseas, including Owndays in Japan. Customers are consumers, with its own manufacturing plant. Headquartered in Gurugram; founded 2010 by Peyush Bansal. Listed on the NSE and BSE (LENSKART) since an IPO in November 2025. Strong consumer brand in India with cricket and celebrity advertising.

wiki.title: Lenskart
wiki.text: Lenskart Solutions Limited is an Indian multinational eyewear company, based in Gurgaon. As a vertically integrated company, it designs, manufactures, distributes, and retails prescription and regular eyewear. It sells its products through its website, a mobile app, and 2,000+ physical stores.

about: Lumen Technologies is a US telecommunications and network services company, providing fiber, internet, security and cloud connectivity to enterprises and public sector clients, after selling its consumer fiber business to AT&T (announced 2025) and its Latin American and European units. Revenue near 13 billion dollars. Headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (LUMN), formerly CenturyLink. Brand known in enterprise networking; naming rights to Lumen Field in Seattle.

wiki.title: Lumen Technologies
wiki.text: Lumen Technologies, Inc. is an American telecommunications company headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. It offers network, security, cloud, voice, and other managed communications services through its fiber optic and copper networks, data centers and cloud computing services. The company has been included in the S&P 600 index since March 2023, and was previously listed among the S&P 500.

about: MiniMax is a Chinese AI company founded in Shanghai in 2021, developing multimodal foundation models such as MiniMax-M2 text, Hailuo video and Speech, offering the Talkie and Hailuo AI apps in consumer markets and APIs for developers. Backed by Alibaba, Tencent and others; listed in Hong Kong in January 2026. Input lists Singapore. Consumer apps reach millions of users globally.

wiki.title: Minimax
wiki.what: Decision rule used for minimizing the possible loss for a worst-case scenario
wiki.text: Minimax is a decision rule used in artificial intelligence, decision theory, combinatorial game theory, statistics, and philosophy for minimizing the possible loss for a worst case scenario. When dealing with gains, it is referred to as "maximin" – to maximize the minimum gain. Originally formulated for several-player zero-sum game theory, covering both the cases where players take alternate moves and those where they make simultaneous moves, it has also been extended to more complex games and to general decision-making in the presence of uncertainty.

wiki.title: MiniMax Group
wiki.text: MiniMax Group Inc. is an artificial intelligence (AI) company based in Shanghai, China. It develops multimodal AI models and consumer applications, including the AI character apps Talkie and Xingye and the video-generation service Hailuo AI. The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026. It is one of China's 6 "AI Tigers".

about: Public Storage is the largest US self-storage operator, with more than 3,000 facilities in the US and a stake in Shurgard in Europe, renting units to households and businesses and selling tenant insurance and retail items. Revenue near 4.7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas (moved from Glendale, California); founded 1972. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (PSA) as a real estate investment trust. Very familiar US consumer brand with orange logo.

wiki.title: Public Storage
wiki.text: Public Storage, headquartered in Frisco, Texas, is a real estate investment trust that invests in self storage. It is the largest brand of self-storage services in the US and owns approximately 9% of the self storage square footage in the U.S. As of December 31, 2024, the company operated 3,073 self-storage facilities containing an aggregate of 221 million net rentable square feet of space. The company also provides insurance services for tenants and manages 307 self storage facilities for other owners. More than 90 percent of Public Storage's revenues are from its self-storage operations; it also provides insurance, packing products.

about: Sabre is a US travel technology company running a global distribution system (GDS) connecting airlines, hotels and car rental firms with travel agencies, plus airline IT and hotel software. Revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Southlake, Texas; founded 1960 as American Airlines' reservation system. Listed on Nasdaq (SABR). Carries high debt. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Sabre Corporation
wiki.text: Sabre Corporation, a travel technology company headquartered in Southlake, Texas, is the largest global distribution systems (GDS) provider for air bookings. The company's primary product, the Sabre Global Distribution System, and others like it, act as neutral intermediaries, connecting travel suppliers like airlines and hotels with travel sellers like agencies. They offer real-time availability and pricing, making them important for corporate travel management.

about: Safe Superintelligence (SSI) is an AI lab founded in 2024 by Ilya Sutskever, Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy with the single goal of building safe superintelligence, with offices in Palo Alto and Tel Aviv. Raised funding at a 32 billion dollar valuation in 2025. Daniel Gross left for Meta, with Sutskever taking over as CEO. No products have been released. Little consumer awareness but high profile among tech investors.

wiki.title: Safe Superintelligence Inc.
wiki.text: Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) is an American artificial intelligence company founded by Ilya Sutskever, the former chief scientist of OpenAI, Daniel Gross, former head of Apple’s AI efforts, and Daniel Levy, an investor and former AI researcher at OpenAI. The company's mission is to focus on safely developing a superintelligence, a computer-based agent capable of surpassing human intelligence.

about: SenseTime is a Chinese artificial intelligence company providing computer vision, facial recognition, large language models (SenseNova) and smart city and automotive AI platforms to governments, enterprises and carmakers. Headquartered in Hong Kong (Sha Tin); founded 2014. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (0020) since 2021. Placed on a US export blacklist in 2019 over surveillance concerns. B2B brand with low consumer awareness and political sensitivity.

wiki.title: SenseTime
wiki.text: SenseTime is a partly state-owned publicly traded artificial intelligence company headquartered in Hong Kong. The company develops technologies including facial recognition, image recognition, object detection, optical character recognition, medical image analysis, video analysis, autonomous driving, and remote sensing. Since 2019, SenseTime has been repeatedly sanctioned by the U.S. government due to allegations that its facial recognition technology has been deployed in the mass surveillance and internment of the Uyghurs and other ethnic and religious minorities. SenseTime denies the allegations.

about: Teleperformance is a French global leader in customer experience outsourcing, running contact centres, digital support, trust and safety, language and AI services for large corporates in more than 90 countries with around 500,000 employees. Revenue near 10 billion euros. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1978. Listed on Euronext Paris (TEP). B2B service provider with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Teleperformance
wiki.text: TP, formerly Teleperformance, is a French multinational business process outsourcing company founded in 1978 with headquarters in France. It provides services for debt collection, telemarketing, customer relationship management, content moderation, and communication.

about: Verisk Analytics supplies data analytics, risk assessment software and underwriting data to insurers and other industries, including property claims tools (Xactimate), ISO insurance forms, climate and catastrophe models and extreme events analytics. Revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey; founded 1971. Listed on Nasdaq (VRSK). B2B brand, well known in the insurance sector with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Verisk Analytics
wiki.what: American data analytics and risk assessment firm
wiki.text: Verisk Analytics, Inc. is an American multinational data analytics and risk assessment firm based in Jersey City, New Jersey. The company's services include fraud prevention, actuarial science, insurance coverage, fire protection, catastrophe and weather risk, and data management.

about: VIRTUS Data Centres is a London-based owner and operator of data centers across the UK and Europe (London, Berlin, Milan, Madrid and others), serving cloud providers and enterprises, with strong investment in AI-ready campuses. Majority owned by ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, a Singapore-based operator. Funding shown is around 2.5 billion pounds or euros including debt. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer visibility.

about: Waters Corporation makes liquid chromatography, mass spectrometry and thermal analysis instruments plus software and consumables, sold to pharmaceutical, biotech, food and chemical laboratories. Revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Milford, Massachusetts; founded 1958. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (WAT). Announced a merger with the biosciences and diagnostics business of Becton Dickinson in 2025. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Bending Spoons is an Italian technology company that buys established digital products and apps, including Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo, AOL, Eventbrite and Meetup, and runs them using a centralised team to cut costs and raise subscription revenue. Also builds its own apps such as Remini and Splice. Headquartered in Milan; founded 2013. Raised funding at a valuation of over 11 billion dollars. Private. Corporate name is little known; its apps have large consumer user bases. Input location data is missing.

wiki.title: Bending Spoons
wiki.text: Bending Spoons S.p.A. is an Italian technology conglomerate founded in 2013. Based in Milan, the company acquires products with existing product‑market fit and manages them for long-term ownership, often increasing revenue and lowering expenses. The company employs full-stack developers to rewrite acquired codebases using artificial intelligence, proprietary tools, and open-source software. On July 1, 2026, the company became public via an initial public offering on the Nasdaq in the United States.

about: Bitfarms is a bitcoin mining company with data centers in Canada, the US (Pennsylvania, Washington state) and Paraguay and Argentina, and it has said it will move toward high-performance computing and AI hosting. Founded 2017; originally based in Toronto, though the input shows New York. Listed on Nasdaq and the Toronto Stock Exchange (BITF). Revenue is driven by bitcoin prices. B2B-style company with little consumer awareness, known among crypto investors.

Crusoe is a Denver-based AI infrastructure company that builds and operates data centers and a GPU cloud for AI training and inference. Starting from flared-gas-powered computing, it now develops large campuses such as the Abilene, Texas site for OpenAI and Oracle's Stargate project. Customers are AI labs and enterprises renting compute capacity. It has raised billions in equity and debt, with valuation reported above $10bn. The input lists the name as Nexus Data Centers, likely a variant. B2B infrastructure with limited consumer awareness but high profile in tech and investor circles.

Scale AI is a San Francisco company that provides data labeling, evaluation and data infrastructure used to train AI models. Its platform, using a managed workforce and software, serves AI labs, large tech firms and the US government, including defence contracts. Founded in 2016 by Alexandr Wang, it was valued at about $14bn after Meta bought a 49% stake for roughly $14.3bn in 2025, and Wang joined Meta. Private. B2B, well known in AI and technology circles but with little consumer awareness.

Aspen Technology (AspenTech) is a Bedford, Massachusetts industrial software company providing process simulation, asset optimisation and AI-based software for energy, chemicals, mining and engineering firms. Customers include oil and gas, chemical and utility companies worldwide, paying licence and subscription fees. Revenue is about $1bn. Emerson Electric took a majority stake in 2022, then bought out the remainder in 2025, taking it private from the Nasdaq (AZPN). B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Aspen Technology
wiki.text: Aspen Technology, Inc., known as AspenTech, is a provider of software and services for the process industries headquartered in Bedford, Massachusetts. AspenTech has 35 offices globally.

about: Telegram is a cloud-based messaging app founded by Pavel Durov, offering chats, large groups, channels, bots, mini apps and a crypto-linked wallet. It reports about one billion monthly active users and earns from Telegram Premium subscriptions, advertising in channels and bond and TON-related activity. Headquartered in Dubai, with a legal presence in the British Virgin Islands. Privately held by Durov, with debt financing raised through bonds. Widely known consumer app with huge usage, notably in Russia, Eastern Europe, India and the Middle East, though brand partnerships are rare.

wiki.title: Telegram
wiki.text: A telegram is a written or printed message, originally sent through telegraphy. The use of the telegrams was popular for social and business correspondence in the latter half of the 19th and the first half of the 20th century. Even in the telephone age, the telegram remained popular, and spawned its own style of writing that in turn persisted in other media. Telegram services still exist today, though the popularity has largely waned, replaced by other forms of text communication.

about: UL Solutions is a safety science company, spun out of Underwriters Laboratories, based in Northbrook, Illinois. It provides testing, inspection, certification, auditing and software services, and the UL mark appears on billions of products such as electrical appliances and batteries. Customers are manufacturers, retailers and regulators worldwide, with revenue around $3bn and about 15,000 employees. IPO on the NYSE (ULS) in April 2024. B2B, but the UL mark is widely recognised on packaging; it has sponsored motorsport.

Viasat is a Carlsbad, California satellite communications company supplying broadband internet through its own geostationary satellites, including ViaSat-3, to consumers, airlines, ships, enterprises and governments, plus defence and secure communications gear. In 2023 it acquired Inmarsat. Revenue is over $4bn and it employs several thousand people. Listed on Nasdaq (VSAT). Largely B2B and government, though consumer satellite internet and in-flight Wi-Fi give it some brand exposure; it has been involved in sports and technology sponsorships.

Digital Asset is a New York blockchain software company that created the Daml smart contract language and the Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain used by banks and financial institutions for tokenisation, settlement and collateral. Customers include banks, asset managers and market infrastructure firms. Its investors include Goldman Sachs, DTCC, Citadel Securities, BNP Paribas and Circle. Private, having raised about $857m. B2B fintech with little public brand awareness.

wiki.title: Digital asset
wiki.text: A digital asset is anything that exists only in digital form and comes with a distinct usage right or distinct permission for use. Data that do not possess those rights are not considered assets.

about: Kitopi is a Dubai-based cloud kitchen company that operates delivery-only kitchens and partners with restaurant brands to prepare food centrally for delivery apps in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the US. It makes money from food-preparation fees and a share of orders. Founded in 2018, it was valued above $1bn in 2022 and has raised about $850m, with backers including Prosus and Cathay Innovation, and restructured after cutting costs. Private. Low consumer visibility, mostly in the restaurant trade and delivery sector.

Ripple is a San Francisco company that provides blockchain-based cross-border payment and stablecoin technology, including RippleNet, Ripple Payments, custody services and the RLUSD stablecoin, plus the XRP Ledger and the XRP token. Customers are banks, payment providers and enterprises in many countries. Founded in 2012, it was valued at about $40bn in a 2025 share sale and has acquired Hidden Road, GTreasury and Rail. Private. Well known in crypto, and it has used sports sponsorship, including a recent US-based stadium and F1-linked marketing.

Hyperliquid Strategies is a New York-based digital asset treasury company formed in 2025 to hold the HYPE token of the Hyperliquid decentralised exchange, financed through a roughly $583m private placement and a merger with Sonnet BioTherapeutics, listed on Nasdaq (PURR). Its income depends on the HYPE token's price and any staking returns, and its investors include Paradigm and others. Public vehicle with no products for consumers. Low consumer awareness, but known in crypto investing.

about: CCC Intelligent Solutions is a Chicago cloud platform for the insurance economy, supplying AI-based software for auto claims estimating, repair workflows, parts and total-loss valuation to insurers, repair shops, carmakers and parts suppliers. It links thousands of businesses in the US. Revenue is over $1bn. Listed on the NYSE (CCCS) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Dragoneer Growth Opportunities. B2B, well known to the claims industry, with no consumer brand awareness.

Cyera is a New York AI-native data security platform that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems, with data security posture management and access controls. Customers are large enterprises, including Fortune 500 firms. Founded in Israel in 2021, it has raised over $1.7bn including a 2026 round and was valued at about $9bn. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand, known to security teams, with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Cyera
wiki.text: Cyera is an American cybersecurity company headquartered in New York City, with a research and development center in Tel Aviv, Israel. It develops data security and artificial intelligence governance software in the cybersecurity category known as data security posture management.

about: Eurofiber is a Dutch digital infrastructure company based in Maarssen, owning and operating fibre networks in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and France. It sells dark fibre, connectivity, data center interconnect, cloud and managed network services to enterprises, telecoms, government and healthcare customers. Owned by infrastructure funds including Antin and Dutch pension capital after a 2023 funding. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Figure AI is a San Jose, California AI robotics company building general-purpose humanoid robots, including Figure 02 and Figure 03, together with its Helix vision-language-action model, for use in factories, logistics and eventually homes. It has run pilots with BMW and raised about $1.85bn, valued around $39bn in a 2025 round, with backers including Microsoft, Nvidia, Jeff Bezos, OpenAI and Intel. Private. High profile in technology media; not yet a mainstream consumer brand.

Fireworks AI is a San Mateo, California inference platform that serves open-source and custom AI models quickly and cheaply to developers and enterprises through APIs, fine-tuning and compute services. It was founded in 2022 by former Meta PyTorch engineers, and customers include Uber, Notion, Cursor and Samsung. Funding is about $250m raised at a valuation near $4bn in 2025. Private. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness.

Flexential is a Centennial, Colorado data center and cloud services provider, operating colocation, managed hosting, cloud, connectivity and disaster recovery services from about 40 data centers across the US. Customers are mid-size and large enterprises and technology firms. It has been owned by GI Partners and Social Capital-style investors, with Churchill Capital-backed ownership since 2021, and is private. B2B infrastructure, no consumer profile.

Joulent is listed by Crunchbase as a Houston, Texas company developing large-scale energy systems, and the input places it in artificial intelligence-related industries. Funding shown is about $1.75bn with the latest round in July 2026. The input does not say what products, customers or owners it has, and the name matches no company I can confidently identify. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Motive is a San Francisco fleet management and driver safety platform, formerly KeepTruckin, offering AI dashcams, electronic logging devices, vehicle telematics, spend management and compliance tools. It serves tens of thousands of fleets in trucking, construction, oil and gas and field services across North America. Valued at $2.85bn in 2022 and raised around $2bn in total. It filed for a US IPO in 2025. B2B brand, widely seen on truck windshields but not a consumer name.

wiki.title: Motive (company)
wiki.text: Motive Technologies, Inc. is a technology company that creates software used by truck companies. Its main product is Hours of Service monitoring using GPS tracking and dashcams.

about: Pinterest is a San Francisco visual discovery platform where users save and organise ideas as pins for shopping, recipes, home, fashion and travel. It has more than 570 million monthly active users and earns from advertising, with revenue near $4bn. Founded in 2010, it listed on the NYSE (PINS) in 2019. Strong consumer social brand with heavy use by women and Gen Z users, and advertiser-focused partnerships rather than sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Pinterest
wiki.text: Pinterest is an American social media service for publishing and discovery of information in the form of digital pinboards. This includes recipes, home, style, motivation, and inspiration on the Internet using image sharing. Pinterest, Inc. was founded by Ben Silbermann, Paul Sciarra, and Evan Sharp, and is headquartered in San Francisco.

about: Reflection AI is a New York frontier AI lab, founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, working on autonomous coding agents and open frontier models. It raised $2bn in October 2025 at an $8bn valuation, led by Nvidia, with 1789 Capital, Lightspeed and others, and is building up open-weight model releases. Private. Known in AI circles, with no consumer products yet.

wiki.title: Reflection AI
wiki.text: Reflection AI is an American artificial intelligence company that develops open foundation models and software agents for AI-assisted software development. Founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, the company initially focused on tools that automate software development. As of June 2026, Reflection's valuation is $25 billion.

about: Skild AI is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania robotics AI start-up, formed in 2023 by Carnegie Mellon roboticists, developing a general-purpose robot brain, Skild Brain, to run on many robot types. It raised about $1.4bn in a January 2026 round at a valuation near $14bn, with SoftBank, Nvidia and Macquarie, and earlier backing from Amazon and Lightspeed. Private. Known in AI and robotics circles; no consumer products.

Thinking Machines Lab is a San Francisco AI research and product company founded in 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, with co-founders including John Schulman. It focuses on collaborative AI systems and released Tinker, a fine-tuning product. It raised $2bn in seed funding in 2025 at a $12bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Nvidia and AMD, and has been reported as raising more at a much higher valuation. Private. Heavily covered in tech media; no consumer products yet.

wiki.title: Thinking Machines Lab
wiki.text: Thinking Machines Lab Inc. is an American artificial intelligence (AI) startup founded by Mira Murati, the former chief technology officer of OpenAI. Their flagship model is Inkling, an open weights large language model.

about: ClickUp is a San Diego cloud work management platform for tasks, docs, chat, goals and AI tools, used by teams from start-ups to enterprises, with millions of users globally. It earns subscription fees and was valued at $4bn after a 2021 round, with total funding of about $660m from investors including Insight Partners, Craft and Tiger Global. Founded 2017. Private. Known to knowledge workers; B2B-leaning brand with low mainstream awareness.

wiki.title: ClickUp
wiki.text: ClickUp is a project management software company that provides an all-in-one platform to improve workplace efficiency and collaboration. The platform's features include tasks, chat, whiteboards, spreadsheets, and document collaboration on a unified platform. It was founded by Zeb Evans and Alex Yurkowski in 2017.

about: MKS Instruments is an Andover, Massachusetts supplier of instruments, subsystems and process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics, advanced materials and life sciences, including vacuum, laser, photonics and power products, many from its 2016 acquisition of Newport and 2022 Atotech deal. Revenue is near $3.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MKSI). B2B industrial technology brand, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: MKS Instruments
wiki.text: MKS Inc. is a technology company that supplies instruments, subsystems, systems, process control technologies, and specialty chemical products used in manufacturing semiconductor chips, printed circuit board, advanced packaging (semiconductor), and specialty industrial applications. The company also provides chemicals and equipment used for creating decorative and functional surface finishes. The company is headquartered in Andover, Massachusetts, with offices and facilities worldwide.

about: Dayforce (formerly Ceridian) is a Minneapolis-based cloud human capital management software company, supplying payroll, HR, time and attendance, benefits and talent tools to mid-market and large employers in North America and abroad. Revenue is above $1.8bn. Thoma Bravo agreed to take it private in 2025 in an $12.3bn deal, after which it left the NYSE (DAY). B2B software with solid HR industry recognition, and little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Dayforce
wiki.text: Dayforce, Inc., formerly Ceridian, is an American human resources software and services company.

about: Clio is a Burnaby, British Columbia cloud legal practice management software company, serving law firms with case management, billing, client intake and AI tools (Clio Manage, Clio Grow, Clio Work), with over 150,000 users. It raised $900m in 2025 at a $5bn valuation and agreed to buy vLex for about $1bn. Founded in 2008. Private. B2B software with strong awareness among lawyers and little in the general public.

wiki.title: Clio
wiki.what: Muse of history in Ancient Greek mythology
wiki.text: In Greek mythology, Clio, also spelled Kleio, Cleio, or Cleo, is the muse of history, or in a few mythological accounts, the muse of lyre-playing.

about: Quantum Computing Inc. is a Hoboken, New Jersey company, listed on Nasdaq (QUBT), developing photonic quantum technologies such as thin-film lithium niobate chips and quantum optics for sensing, computing and security. It has raised capital through private placements, giving it a cash pile near $1.5bn. Revenue is tiny. Speculative technology company with a strong retail-investor following but no consumer products.

wiki.title: Quantum computing
wiki.what: Computer hardware technology that uses quantum mechanics
wiki.text: A quantum computer is a computer that represents and processes information using quantum states. Quantum computations exploit phenomena such as superposition, interference, and entanglement. Quantum computers have the potential to complete some calculations exponentially faster than classical computers. For example, a large-scale quantum computer could break widely used encryption schemes and aid physicists in performing physical simulations. However, current hardware implementations of quantum computation are largely experimental and suitable for only certain specialized tasks.

about: Rippling is a San Francisco workforce management platform combining HR, payroll, IT device management, spend and benefits in one system, serving tens of thousands of businesses, from start-ups to mid-size firms. Founded in 2016 by Parker Conrad, it raised $450m in 2025 at a $16.8bn valuation, led by Elad Gil and Baillie Gifford. Private. B2B software with high recognition among HR and start-up leaders, and an active marketing and sponsorship presence in sports, including with F1 teams.

wiki.title: Rippling
wiki.text: In computer science, more particularly in automated theorem proving, rippling is a group of meta-level heuristics, developed primarily in the Mathematical Reasoning Group in the School of Informatics at the University of Edinburgh, and most commonly used to guide inductive proofs in automated theorem proving systems. Rippling may be viewed as a restricted form of rewrite system, where special object level annotations are used to ensure fertilization upon the completion of rewriting, with a measure decreasing requirement ensuring termination for any set of rewrite rules and expression.

wiki.title: Rippling (company)
wiki.text: Rippling is a privately owned international software company. Launched in 2017 in San Francisco, California, it operates a cloud-based software platform that allows businesses to manage their HR, finances, and IT matters, and also has AI features to automate administrative tasks and provide data and analysis.

about: TierPoint is a St. Louis-based US data center and cloud services provider offering colocation, managed hosting, disaster recovery and cybersecurity from about 30 data centers, serving mid-market enterprises. It is backed by Brightstar and Wafra, with large debt facilities (raised $2.4bn including financing), and acquired several smaller operators. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Paxos is a New York blockchain infrastructure company and regulated trust company founded in 2012. It issues regulated stablecoins, including Pax Dollar (USDP), PayPal's PYUSD and Global Dollar (USDG), and provides tokenization, crypto brokerage and custody infrastructure to banks, fintechs and asset managers such as PayPal, Interactive Brokers and Mastercard. Chartered by the New York Department of Financial Services. B2B infrastructure, known mainly in finance and crypto, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Paxos
wiki.what: Greek island in the Ionian Sea
wiki.text: Paxos is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, lying just south of Corfu. As a group with the nearby island of Antipaxos and adjoining islets, it is also called by the plural form Paxi or Paxoi. The main town and the seat of the municipality is Gaios. The smallest of the seven main Ionian Islands, Paxos has an area of 25.3 square kilometres (9.8 sq mi), while the municipality has an area of 30.121 km2 (11.630 sq mi) and a population of 2,466.

wiki.title: Paxos (company)
wiki.text: Paxos Trust Company, N.A. is a blockchain infrastructure company, stablecoin issuer, and chartered national bank headquartered in New York City. The company provides digital asset brokerage, issuance, custody, and settlement services to enterprise clients in financial services. Paxos has also issued multiple U.S. dollar-backed stablecoins, including PayPal USD (PYUSD), Pax Dollar (USDP), and Global Dollar (USDG). ItBit, a bitcoin exchange run by Paxos, was the first bitcoin exchange to be licensed by the New York State Department of Financial Services, granting the company the ability to be the custodian and exchange for customers in the Unit

about: Nothing is a London-based consumer electronics company founded in 2020 by Carl Pei, co-founder of OnePlus. It makes Nothing Phone smartphones, Nothing Ear and CMF by Nothing audio and wearables, known for transparent design and its Glyph light interface, and is building AI-led devices and the Essential feature in its OS. Sells directly and through retail partners in dozens of markets, mainly Europe, India and the US. It has raised about $450 million. Growing design-led consumer brand with strong youth and tech awareness.

wiki.title: Nothing
wiki.what: Complete absence of anything; the opposite of everything
wiki.text: Nothing, no-thing, or no thing is the complete absence of anything, as the opposite of something and an antithesis of everything. The concept of nothing has been a matter of philosophical debate since at least the 5th century BCE. Early Greek philosophers argued that it was impossible for nothing to "exist". The atomists allowed nothing but only in the spaces between the invisibly small atoms. For them, all space was filled with atoms. Aristotle took the view that there exists matter and there exists space, a receptacle into which matter objects can be placed. This became the paradigm for classical scientists of the modern age, like Isaac New

wiki.title: Nothing (company)
wiki.text: Nothing Technology Limited is a British consumer electronics company headquartered in London. It was co-founded in 2020 by Carl Pei, alongside Akis Evangelidis, David Sanmartín García, Steven Gao, and Levi Li, among others. The company develops smartphones, audio products, and related software, positioning itself as a design-focused challenger brand.

about: SK Horizon is a Seoul-based AI data center infrastructure company (AIDC). The Crunchbase description says it is an AI data center infrastructure company, with an unusually large reported funding figure (about 3.08 trillion Korean won, August 2026). It is likely related to the SK Group, but ownership and details are not confirmed by the input. B2B infrastructure. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: SK Horizon is an Al data center (AIDC) infrastructure company.

about: Wistron Corporation is a Taipei-based electronics manufacturing and design company, founded in 2001 as a spin-off of Acer. It builds laptops, servers, networking and medical equipment for brands such as Dell, HP and Lenovo, plus AI servers via the Wiwynn subsidiary. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3231) with revenue in the tens of billions of dollars. B2B contract manufacturing, little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Wistron
wiki.text: Wistron Corporation is an electronics manufacturer based in Taiwan. It was the manufacturing arm of Acer Inc. before being spun off in 2000. As an original design manufacturer, the company designs and manufactures products for other companies to sell under their brand name. Wistron products include notebook and desktop computers, servers, storage, LCD TVs, handheld devices, and devices and equipment for medical applications.

about: Flex (Flex Ltd.) is a global contract electronics manufacturer and supply chain company, historically Flextronics, with operational headquarters in Austin, Texas and legal home in Singapore. It designs and manufactures products for automotive, healthcare, industrial, communications and data center clients, including power and cooling for AI data centers, with about $26 billion revenue and some 150,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (FLEX). B2B, low brand awareness among consumers.

wiki.title: Flex Ltd.
wiki.text: Flex Ltd. is a multinational manufacturing company. It is the world's third largest global electronics manufacturing services (EMS), original design manufacturer (ODM) company by revenue, behind only Pegatron. Flex's U.S. corporate headquarters are located in Austin, Texas, while the legal domicile is located in Singapore. The company has manufacturing operations in over 30 countries, and employs about 172,000 people.

about: Bird is the Amsterdam-based cloud communications platform formerly called MessageBird, founded in 2011 by Robert Vis. It provides APIs and software for SMS, voice, WhatsApp and email messaging, a customer-engagement inbox and a conversational AI offering, serving thousands of businesses worldwide. Revenue comes from usage and subscriptions. Backed by investors such as Accel and Y Combinator, with a peak valuation near $3 billion and about $1.5 billion raised. B2B, known among developers and marketers, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Bird
wiki.what: Warm-blooded animals with wings and feathers
wiki.text: Birds are vertebrate animals constituting the class Aves, characterised by feathers, toothless beaked jaws, the laying of hard-shelled eggs, a high metabolic rate, a four-chambered heart, and a strong yet lightweight skeleton. They are warm-blooded, live worldwide, and range in size from the 5.5 cm (2.2 in) bee hummingbird to the 2.8 m common ostrich. There are over 11,000 living species of birds, classified in 44 orders. More than half of the world's bird species are passerine or "perching" birds. Nearly all birds have wings whose development varies according to the life style of each species. Wings, which are modified forelimbs, gave birds

about: D-Wave Quantum is a Palo Alto, California and Burnaby, Canada-based quantum computing company, founded in 1999, that builds annealing quantum computers (Advantage systems) and gate-model research, offered via cloud (Leap) and on-premise to enterprises, researchers and governments. Listed on the NYSE (QBTS) since going public via SPAC in 2022. Customers include Davidson Technologies, NTT Docomo and Ford Otosan. B2B deep tech with strong retail-investor interest but little brand awareness among the general public.

Flapping Airplanes is a US artificial intelligence research lab described as a startup in AI research. The input shows reported funding of about $1.18 billion and the company is classed in artificial intelligence. No further reliable detail on its products, customers or backers can be given from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Flapping Airplanesis anprh artificial intelligence research...

about: Guidewire Software is a San Mateo, California software company, founded in 1998, providing the core platform for property and casualty insurers: policy, billing and claims systems (InsuranceSuite), plus data analytics and cloud services. Customers are insurance carriers in over 40 countries. Listed on NYSE (GWRE) with annual revenue near $1 billion. B2B enterprise software, with low consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Guidewire Software
wiki.text: Guidewire Software, Inc., commonly Guidewire, is an American software company based in San Mateo, California. It offers an industry platform for property and casualty (P&C) insurance carriers in the U.S. and worldwide.

about: Keyfactor is a Cleveland, Ohio provider of digital identity and machine identity management, specialising in public key infrastructure (PKI), certificate lifecycle and secure code signing. Customers are enterprises across financial services, healthcare and manufacturing worldwide. Owned by Insight Partners and in 2025 acquired by Thoma Bravo; it has raised about $1.2 billion in funding. B2B cybersecurity, little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Keyfactoroffers secure digital identity management solution...

about: Kpler is a Brussels-headquartered data and analytics firm founded in 2014, providing real-time tracking of commodity flows across oil, gas, shipping and agriculture, using satellite and vessel data. Customers include traders, banks, governments and energy companies. It acquired Spire Maritime and MarineTraffic, and raised funds from Eurazeo and others, with a valuation near $1 billion or more. B2B data, little consumer brand awareness.

Megaport is a Brisbane-based Australian provider of elastic network infrastructure, offering software-defined networking services such as Megaport Cloud Router and Virtual Edge that connect enterprises to cloud providers and data centers. Founded in 2013, it is listed on the ASX (MP1) and has a global footprint of over 900 data centers. Customers are enterprises, cloud providers and carriers. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Neuralink is a Fremont, California neurotechnology company founded in 2016 by Elon Musk and others that develops implantable brain-computer interfaces (the N1 chip, 'Telepathy') for people with paralysis, aiming at restoring movement and communication. The first human implant was in 2024, with trials across several countries. Raised about $1.3 billion from investors including Founders Fund, with a reported valuation of several billion dollars. Private company with high public awareness because of Musk but no consumer product yet.

wiki.title: Neuralink
wiki.text: Neuralink Corp. is an American neurotechnology company that is developing implantable brain–computer interfaces (BCIs). It was founded by Elon Musk and a team of eight scientists and engineers. Neuralink was launched in 2016 and first publicly reported in March 2017. The company is based in Fremont, California, with plans to build a three-story building with office and manufacturing space in Del Valle, about 10 miles east of Gigafactory Texas, Tesla's headquarters and manufacturing plant.

about: Oklo is a Santa Clara, California advanced nuclear power company designing small modular fission reactors (the Aurora powerhouse) to supply electricity and heat to data centers and industrial customers, plus fuel recycling. Founded in 2013, its backers include Sam Altman, who was its chairman until 2025. Listed on NYSE (OKLO) after a 2024 SPAC merger with AltC. Pre-revenue, with project sites in Idaho. B2B energy with high investor attention, little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Oklo
wiki.what: Region containing uranium ore in Haut-Ogooué, Gabon
wiki.text: Oklo is a geological region near Franceville in the Haut-Ogooué Province of Gabon. Several natural nuclear fission reactors were discovered in the uranium mines in the region in 1972.

about: Persistent Systems is a Pune-based Indian IT services and product engineering company, founded in 1990, offering software development, digital engineering, cloud, data and AI services to clients in banking, healthcare, software and telecom, mainly in the US. It has over 23,000 employees and revenue of around $1.4 billion. Listed on the NSE and BSE (PERSISTENT). B2B, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Persistent Systems
wiki.text: Persistent Systems Ltd is an Indian multinational technology company based in Pune. Founded in 1990, it provides information technology and software engineering services.

about: Quantinuum is a quantum computing company headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado and Cambridge, UK, formed in 2021 from Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum. It builds trapped-ion quantum computers (H-series, Helios), plus software such as InQuanto, and quantum-secure cryptography. Majority-owned by Honeywell, valued at about $10 billion after a 2025 raise; it filed for a public listing. Customers are enterprises, governments and researchers. B2B deep tech, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Quantinuum
wiki.text: Quantinuum is a quantum computing company formed by the merger of Cambridge Quantum and Honeywell Quantum Solutions. The company's H-Series trapped-ion quantum computers set the highest quantum volume to date of 33,554,432 in September 2025. This architecture supports all-to-all qubit connectivity, allowing entangled states to be created between all qubits, and enables a high fidelity of quantum states.

about: SandboxAQ is a Palo Alto, California company spun out of Alphabet in 2022 by Jack Hidary, building AI and quantum technology products for drug and materials discovery, cybersecurity and navigation (AQNav). It sells software to enterprises and governments in life sciences, chemicals and defence. Raised about $1.5 billion, including from Google, Salesforce, Nvidia and Ray Dalio's fund, at a valuation of $5.75 billion in 2025. B2B deep tech with low consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Jack Hidary
wiki.text: Jack D. Hidary is the CEO of AI and quantum technology company SandboxAQ.

about: Supabase is a San Francisco-based open-source backend platform for application developers, offering a Postgres database, authentication, storage and real-time APIs, often described as an open-source Firebase alternative. Founded in 2020, it serves developers and startups, with usage-based and subscription revenue. Raised about $1.2 billion in total, including a recent round at a multi-billion valuation. B2B developer tool, strong with developers but little consumer awareness.

ClickHouse is a database company, headquartered in the US (San Francisco Bay Area), that offers the open-source ClickHouse column-oriented analytics database and a managed cloud service. It spun out of Yandex in 2021 and serves customers such as Cloudflare, Uber and eBay for real-time analytics and observability. Raised about $1.15 billion with a valuation of roughly $6 billion. B2B developer infrastructure, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: ClickHouse
wiki.text: ClickHouse is an open-source column-oriented DBMS for online analytical processing (OLAP) that allows users to generate analytical reports using structured query language (SQL) queries in real-time. ClickHouse Inc. is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with the subsidiary, ClickHouse B.V., based in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

about: Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs) is a Paris-based AI start-up co-founded by Yann LeCun after he left Meta, focused on research into world models and advanced machine intelligence. It reportedly raised close to 890 million euros in early funding. It has no commercial consumer product yet. Research-stage company, known in AI circles through LeCun, with little brand awareness among the public.
cb_desc: Advanced Machine Intelligence develops artificial intelligence...

about: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas robotics company, spun out of the University of Texas, that designs and builds general-purpose humanoid robots, notably Apollo, for logistics and manufacturing. Customers and partners include Mercedes-Benz, GXO and Jabil, with Google DeepMind as an AI partner. Raised about $964 million, including a $403 million Series A in 2025. B2B robotics startup with growing media attention but low consumer awareness.

Bedrock Robotics is a US company that develops autonomous robotics systems for heavy construction equipment, retrofitting excavators and other machines for autonomous operation on building sites. Customers are construction contractors. Founded in 2024 by former Waymo engineers, it has raised about $950 million. B2B construction technology, little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Bedrock Robotics develops autonomous robotics systems...

wiki.title: Bedrock Robotics
wiki.text: Bedrock Robotics is an American company, based in San Francisco, that develops sensor, computing and machine-learning systems to automate heavy construction equipment, beginning with excavators. It was founded in 2024 by former Waymo engineers.

about: CAIS is a New York-based financial technology platform, formerly CAIS Group, that gives independent financial advisers access to alternative investments such as hedge funds, private equity and real estate funds, with tools for subscription, reporting and education. Founded in 2009, it raised about $916 million and counts Apollo and Franklin Templeton among its investors. B2B, with low consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: CAIS is a financial technology platform that provides..

about: Claroty is a New York-based cybersecurity company, founded in 2015 in Israel, that protects extended Internet of Things (XIoT) assets, such as industrial, healthcare and building systems, for enterprises with operational technology. Customers include manufacturers, hospitals and utilities. Backed by Bessemer, Rockwell, Siemens and Schneider Electric with funding of about $940 million and a valuation above $3 billion. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Grafana Labs is a New York-based observability software company that created the open-source Grafana dashboard tool and sells the Grafana Cloud platform with Loki, Tempo and Mimir for monitoring metrics, logs and traces. Founded in 2014 by Raj Dutt, it has more than 7,000 customers including Bloomberg and Salesforce, and has raised over $1 billion, with a valuation around $6 billion. B2B developer tooling, with strong awareness among engineers but not consumers.

Ineffable Intelligence is a UK-based artificial intelligence start-up reportedly founded by David Silver, formerly of Google DeepMind, to build machine learning systems that learn from experience. The input shows reported funding of about $1.1 billion and a London base. It has no commercial products on the market. Research-stage company, known mainly in AI circles. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Ineffable Intelligence develops machine learning systems tha...

about: Nexthink is a Lausanne, Switzerland and Boston-based software company, founded in 2004, offering a digital employee experience platform that monitors laptops and applications so IT teams can find and fix issues. Customers are large enterprises worldwide, including many Fortune 500 firms. Backed by Vista Equity Partners, GV and Highland Europe, with funding of about $1.1 billion and a valuation above $3 billion. B2B software, little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Nexthink
wiki.text: Nexthink is a Swiss software company specializing in digital employee experience (DEX) management. Founded in 2004, the company provides IT teams with real-time analytics, automation, and employee feedback tools to monitor and enhance the digital workplace experience.

about: Physical Intelligence is a San Francisco AI company, founded in 2024 by researchers including Karol Hausman, Sergey Levine and Chelsea Finn, that is developing foundation models for general-purpose robot control (the pi0 and pi0.5 models). It has raised about $1.07 billion from investors such as Thrive Capital, Lux and Bezos Expeditions, at a multi-billion valuation. Research-stage B2B company with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Theory of multiple intelligences
wiki.text: The theory of multiple intelligences (MI) posits that human intelligence is not a single general ability but comprises various distinct modalities, such as linguistic, logical-mathematical, musical, and spatial intelligences. Introduced in Howard Gardner's book Frames of Mind: The Theory of Multiple Intelligences (1983), this framework has gained popularity among educators who accordingly develop varied teaching strategies purported to cater to different student strengths.

about: V.tal is a Brazilian neutral digital infrastructure company, created in 2021 by BTG Pactual with Oi's fiber network, which offers wholesale fibre, backhaul and network services to telecom operators across Brazil. Based in Rio de Janeiro, it holds one of the biggest fibre networks in Latin America. Customers are operators like TIM, Claro and Vivo, and it reported over $1 billion in funding. B2B infrastructure, with little consumer brand awareness.

Waabi is a Toronto-based autonomous trucking technology company, founded in 2021 by Raquel Urtasun, a University of Toronto professor and former Uber ATG chief scientist. It builds the Waabi Driver using a generative AI simulator, working with Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Uber Freight. Funding is about $1.03 billion including a 2026 round. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Waabi
wiki.text: Waabi Innovations Inc., doing business as Waabi, is an artificial intelligence company developing self-driving technology. It is headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. The company was founded and is led by Raquel Urtasun, a University of Toronto professor and formerly chief scientist and head of research and development at Uber's Advanced Technologies Group.

about: Xanadu is a Toronto-based quantum computing company, founded in 2016 by Christian Weedbrook, building photonic quantum computers (Aurora) and the PennyLane quantum software library. It serves researchers, enterprises and governments, and announced a plan to list through a SPAC merger with Crane Harbor in 2025. Funding about $986 million reported. B2B deep tech with limited consumer awareness.

Tekion is a San Ramon, California cloud-native software platform for automotive retail, founded in 2016 by Jay Vijayan (ex-Tesla), offering dealer management systems, CRM, finance and service tools with AI to car dealerships, OEMs and service shops. It has raised about $635 million at a valuation of about $4 billion. Customers are dealers and automakers across North America. B2B software, with low consumer brand awareness.

Zebra Technologies is a US enterprise technology company headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois and listed on Nasdaq (ZBRA). It makes barcode scanners and printers, RFID readers, mobile computers, tablets and machine vision, serving retail, logistics, healthcare and manufacturing customers worldwide with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Its Zebra MotionWorks tracking solution is used by the NFL to track players. Founded 1969. B2B technology brand, partly visible via sports data partnerships.

wiki.title: Zebra Technologies
wiki.text: Zebra Technologies Corporation (ZBR), commonly known as Zebra, is an American multinational technology conglomerate corporation, specializing in smart data capture systems.

about: Dataminr is a New York-based real-time event detection company founded in 2009 that uses AI to scan public data such as social media, news and sensor feeds and alerts corporate and public-sector clients to emerging risks. Customers include news organisations, governments, banks and large corporates, who pay for its alert subscriptions. It has raised hundreds of millions of dollars at a valuation of roughly 4 billion dollars. B2B brand with moderate profile in media, security and risk circles.

wiki.title: Dataminr
wiki.what: Artificial intelligence platform for event and risk detection
wiki.text: Dataminr is an artificial intelligence company. The company's private sector product, Dataminr Pulse, is used by corporations to monitor real-time events, and to aid with crisis response by providing playbooks, messaging tools and post-event documentation. Dataminr's First Alert technology is used by first responders, such as those helping to provide aid during natural disasters and other emergency events. Similar applications can be achieved by social surveillance vendors such as Feedly, Geofeedia, Raven Pack, Semantic Visions, ShadowDragon, and Signal AI.

about: Figma is a collaborative interface design tool used by product teams to design, prototype and share web and mobile apps in the browser, plus FigJam whiteboards and Dev Mode. Headquartered in San Francisco, it was founded in 2012 and listed on the NYSE (FIG) in 2025, after Adobe's 20 billion dollar bid was cancelled in 2023. Customers are designers and developers at companies of all sizes, paying subscriptions. Revenue is above 700 million dollars. Strong brand among creative and tech professionals.

wiki.title: Figma
wiki.text: Figma is a collaborative web-based application for user interface design. It supports the design of mobile apps, websites, and illustrations, with 13 million users as of 2025. It is the product of the eponymous Figma, Inc., founded in 2012 by Dylan Field and Evan Wallace.

about: KoBold Metals is a Berkeley, California mineral exploration company using AI and geoscience data to find critical minerals such as copper, nickel, cobalt and lithium for the battery industry. Founded 2018, backed by Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Jeff Bezos, it holds a major copper project in Zambia (Mingomba) and explores in Canada, Australia and the US. Customers are mining and battery supply chain buyers. B2B startup with a strong investor profile, not a consumer brand.
